analysis.title: TSMC (2330.TW) Earnings review: 3Q26 inline but 4Q26 GM came in slightly softer; AI demand outlook shows no signs of slowdown; reiterate Buy
key_insights: TSMC raised its 2026 revenue growth outlook to around 44% YoY in USD terms, from slightly above 40%, on continued strong AI/HPC demand.

3Q26 GM of 66.4% fell 1.3ppt QoQ on dilution from the initial N2 ramp, and was 1.1ppt below GSe. 4Q26 GM is guided to 65-67%, a midpoint of 66.0%, down a further 40bps on continued N2 dilution and overseas fabs.

Management said AI demand is extremely robust, with no sign of slowdown, and still far exceeds supply. It did not formally update the long-term AI accelerator revenue CAGR but indicated it will probably be higher.

Drivers cited for AI demand: agentic AI lifting CPU demand (excluded from TSMC's AI accelerator definition), open-source model adoption lowering the barrier to AI use, continued networking chip demand, and TSMC's own checks showing CSPs are well prepared on US data center build and power supply.
N2 capacity is guided to be more than double in 2027, the first time management has given this guidance.

TSMC announced an additional 3nm fab expansion in Tainan with volume production in 1H28. This adds to the ongoing Tainan N3 expansion (ramp 1H27), Arizona fab 2 (ramp 3Q27, slightly ahead of prior schedule), Japan fab 2 (ramp 2028) and continued N5-to-N3 tool conversion.
TSMC is evaluating Texas as an additional US site and is in discussion with one customer building Terafab about using that capacity. TSMC said its principle is to run the fab by itself.

Management now expects overseas fab dilution of closer to 2% for full-year 2026 (previously 2-3%), but reiterated it will widen to 3-4% in the latter part of the five-year period as more US fabs ramp. Management said there is 'no ceiling' for long-term profitability but no dramatic increase will happen overnight.

2026 CapEx guidance is unchanged at US$60-64bn. Management reiterated that 2026-2028 CapEx will be significantly higher than the prior three years and that revenue growth should outpace CapEx growth. GS keeps CapEx at US$64bn/85bn/98bn for 2026E/27E/28E.

Management expressed confidence in its technology lead. It is in volume production at 5x reticle size in advanced packaging, with 9x and 14x in development. High NA EUV adoption is planned for 2030, which management does not see as a disadvantage. A14 (volume production 2028) is expected to be a bigger node than N2, with customer engagement already above N2's at the same stage.

GS cut GM estimates to 66.6%/66.8%/67.7% for 2026-2028E from 67.2%/67.5%/67.8%, and raised 2026/27/28E EPS by 1.4%/0.0%/0.6% on stronger 4Q26 revenue guidance and the higher 2026 growth outlook, partly offset by the lower GM.
GS reiterates Buy and keeps the 12m TP at NT$3,300 (TSM ADR US$660), based on 22x target P/E on 2027E EPS. The TP implies 35.2% upside for the local share and 53.5% for the ADR.

market_movers.rationale: Reiterate Buy on the ADR with a $660 TP (22x 2027E EPS, USD/TWD 30.0, 20% ADR premium). GS cites AI demand ahead of supply, a structural technology lead, and a raised 2026 revenue outlook, partly offset by softer GM.

sector_views.rationale: GS sees TSMC as the key AI enabler in its Taiwan semis coverage, given leading-edge node and CoWoS advanced packaging leadership.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 revenue NT$1,494.2bn (US$46.72bn), reported, up 17.6% QoQ and 50.9% YoY. Above GSe by 0.8% and consensus by 2.1%, and above the high end of guidance in USD terms.
3Q26 EPS NT$29.43, reported, up 8.0% QoQ and 68.7% YoY. Above GSe NT$29.07 by 1.2% and consensus NT$28.38 by 3.7%. Excluding the NT$2.24 one-off gain from the VIS disposal in 2Q26, EPS grew 18% QoQ.

3Q26 GM 66.4% reported, 1.1ppt below GSe 67.5% and 0.1ppt below consensus 66.5%, in the upper half of the 65-67% guidance. OpM 58.7% beat the high end of the 56-58% guidance on OpEx stable at 7.8% of revenue.

3Q26 technology mix: N2 was 8% of wafer revenue (3% in 2Q26), N3 33% (30%), and advanced nodes (7nm and below) 79% (77%). HPC rose 22% QoQ to 68% of revenue, and smartphone rose 10% QoQ to 21%. Inventory days fell 5 days QoQ to 82.
4Q26 guidance: revenue US$52.3-54.3bn (+14% QoQ at midpoint, at TWD/USD 31.8) versus GSe +11.0% QoQ. GM 65-67% (midpoint 66.0% vs GSe 67.3% and consensus 66.1%). OpM 56.5-58.5%.

trade_ideas.description: Buy TSMC (2330.TW) and the TSM ADR, 12m TP NT$3,300 / US$660
trade_ideas.rationale: Technology leadership and execution position TSMC to capture structural AI/HPC growth, with AI demand still ahead of supply.
trade_ideas.risk: Weaker end-demand hurting utilization, slower node migration, an AI investment slowdown, poor yields, stronger competition, or unfavorable FX and cost increases.

risk_factors: Further deterioration in end-demand recovery impacting capacity utilization.
Slowdown in AI investment, resulting in lower long-term semiconductor content growth.
Poor yields or execution, resulting in worse-than-expected profitability.
Stronger competition, resulting in ASP and profitability erosion.
Unfavorable FX trend or higher-than-expected cost increases weighing on the margin outlook.
Near-term GM pressure from the N2 ramp and overseas fab dilution, widening to 3-4% later in the five-year period.

tension_points.bull_case: Revenue guidance is well above expectations (4Q26 +14% QoQ vs GSe +11%), the 2026 growth outlook is up to ~44%, AI demand exceeds supply, and management says there is 'no ceiling' on long-term profitability.
tension_points.bear_case: 3Q26 GM was 1.1ppt below GSe, 4Q26 GM guidance is 1.3ppt below GSe, and overseas fab dilution is expected to widen to 3-4% later in the five-year period.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A slowdown in AI investment or poor N2 yields and execution, which the report lists as key downside risks.
